title: Feature Overcorrelation in Deep Graph Neural Networks: A New Perspective

problem.claim: Deep graph neural networks suffer performance degradation associated with oversmoothing and highly indistinguishable learned node representations.

contributions.claim: Frames performance degradation in deep GNNs through the perspective of feature overcorrelation.
Studies feature overcorrelation empirically and theoretically, reporting its existence in deeper GNNs and potential reasons leading to it.
Introduces DeCorr, a general framework intended to reduce feature correlation by encouraging GNNs to encode less redundant information.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present feature overcorrelation as a new perspective on deep GNN performance degradation and propose DeCorr as a general framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report empirical and theoretical evidence for feature overcorrelation in deeper GNNs and potential reasons for it.
The authors report extensive experiments showing that DeCorr can enable deeper GNNs.
The authors report that DeCorr is complementary to existing techniques addressing oversmoothing.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs have achieved success in applications including recommendation and drug discovery.
Oversmoothing is identified as a key issue limiting deep GNN performance and making node representations highly indistinguishable.
The paper introduces feature overcorrelation as another perspective on performance degradation.
Empirical and theoretical study reports the existence of feature overcorrelation and potential reasons for it.
DeCorr is proposed to reduce feature correlation, with experiments reported to enable deeper GNNs and complement oversmoothing techniques.

source_observation.claim: The paper links deep-GNN degradation to feature overcorrelation and redundant encoded information.

interpretation.claim: Performance problems in deep representation models may involve redundancy or correlation structure beyond the commonly recognized failure mode.

application.claim: When deepening representation models, inspect feature correlation and consider mechanisms that explicitly reduce redundant information.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy transfers beyond GNNs or across specific datasets and architectures.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, architectures, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not provide the theoretical formulation or proof details for feature overcorrelation.
The abstract does not describe DeCorr's implementation or computational overhead.
